subject: Fluoride Ban - D2
comment: Dear Councilman Puy, I am dismayed to see that Gov. Cox signed HB81, prohibiting the addition of fluoride into municipal water sources, into law. Given that Salt Lake City residents voted to add fluoride into our water, is this a law the city could bring a lawsuit against? I understand there are some health risks in higher concentrations, and I am aware of the 2019 incident in Sandy. But I am also familiar with the science that strongly suggests far more benefits than risks, and I have noticed a real improvement in my own dental health since moving here ten years ago. Anything that we can do to push back against this legislative overreach would be appreciated. If it would be helpful, I would also be willing to come to a city council meeting to express my concerns (though I'm definitely not an expert, just a concerned and well-informed citizen). Thank you, Lisa Christensen

subject: April 15th Public Hearing (Item B1) | Public Comment
comment: Dear City Council Members, Local West Jordan childcare providers are writing to express their strong support for the Boost Program in Salt Lake City and to urge you to approve funding to expand this vital initiative to their fellow childcare owners in SLC. She makes sure I have everything I need, responds quickly, and continues to make my job so much easier. Upwards has been an amazing support for my daycare." Veronica Jones, Twine Early Learning Center (West Jordan, UT) "The services provided have significantly enhanced our operations, allowing us to streamline processes and improve customer satisfaction. The TA reimbursement has been invaluable, as it has enabled us to build employee morale." Jessica Sheffield, Bright Start Preschool (West Jordan, UT) "As a busy mom and childcare in-home business owner, I can confirm that having Upwards has made a huge impact on my life. Upwards has saved me time so I can focus more on what I love while still making it possible to provide this service to families. I have appreciated this program a lot, and it has taken one stress off my plate as a mom and childcare owner." Brandiny Martinez, Diny's Munchkins Bilingual Daycare (West Jordan, UT) "I've had a really good experience with Upwards! Alex Estrada has helped me navigate through the app and its awesome features, especially the activity planning, which has been such a big help. I know life as a daycare provider gets busy, but Alex continues to check up on me, sending me helpful resources. I truly appreciate her and the Upwards team!" Thank you very much for your service to our community! Sincerely- Richrd Hendron

subject: Homeless Issues Homeless issues
comment: My name is Sergey Krasovskiy, and I am the co-owner of Forest Rentals, LLC, which is located in the District 5 area of SLC. I am writing to bring your attention to the increasing issue of homelessness and trespassing in the Liberty Wells neighborhood, specifically at our property located at REDACTED. Over the past couple of years, we have observed a significant decline in the safety and security of the area. Previously, these issues were far less frequent, but recently, they have escalated, creating ongoing challenges for property owners and residents. Just recently, our property manager encountered unauthorized individuals trespassing on our private property and unlawfully occupying our vacant units. While police were called and removed them, this has become a recurring issue that is affecting the overall safety and desirability of our community. The persistent presence of homeless individuals in and around our property has led to heightened safety concerns for tenants and residents. This issue has resulted in declining occupancy rates, as potential tenants are deterred by the risks associated with trespassing and unauthorized encampments. Beyond personal safety concerns, the deteriorating security of the area negatively impacts property values, making it more difficult for landlords to maintain and invest in their properties. If this trend continues, the long-term economic impact will extend beyond property owners—declining property values result in lower tax revenues for the city and state, ultimately affecting funding for essential public services. Despite our best efforts to secure our property and work with local law enforcement, addressing the issue has been challenging. The current enforcement mechanisms are not sufficient to prevent repeated incidents of trespassing, and property owners lack adequate support in dealing with these situations effectively. Even when trespassers are taken into custody, they are released almost immediately, allowing them to return and continue their unlawful activities without consequence. This lack of accountability sends the message that trespassing and related offenses carry no real repercussions, further exacerbating the problem. We understand that homelessness is a complex issue that requires compassionate and sustainable solutions. However, it is also essential to ensure that property owners and residents feel safe in their homes and that property values are not eroded due to ongoing trespassing and security concerns. We urge you to consider measures that will: 1. Improve enforcement protocols for preventing and addressing trespassing on private property. 2. Increase police presence and intervention in areas affected by trespassing and related criminal activities. 3. Develop programs that offer better support and housing solutions for homeless individuals, reducing the need for them to seek shelter on private property. 4. Implement policies that protect property owners from financial losses due to declining occupancy rates caused by persistent homelessness issues, such as financial reimbursements or tax incentives for affected landlords. 5. Strengthen community safety initiatives to ensure that residents feel secure in their neighborhoods and public spaces. 6. Reform current laws to impose actual consequences on those who trespass and engage in unlawful activities, rather than allowing them to be immediately released without any accountability. We believe that a collaborative approach involving local government, law enforcement, and property owners is necessary to find an effective resolution. We would appreciate the opportunity to discuss this matter further and explore potential legislative or policy changes that could help address this growing concern. If no action is taken and the situation continues to worsen, we will have no choice but to escalate this issue to local and state media to expose the ongoing inaction that is negatively affecting law-abiding property owners and residents. This is not an issue that can be ignored any longer. Please let us know a convenient time when we might be able to meet or speak with you and your team. We are also in discussions with other landlords and residents in the area who share these concerns and are prepared to collectively advocate for necessary changes. Thank you for your time and attention to this matter. We look forward to your response and to working together on solutions that benefit both the community and property owners alike. Sincerely, Sergey Krasovskiy, Forest Rentals, LLC

subject: An informative day... Numbers are the story
comment: Wayne and Andrew, A trial survey showed that 90% of the people in our program were raised as Catholics or as members of the LDS community. 65-70% were or are LDS. 70% were born in Utah. 66% of those who moved here from another state were LDS. Almost 70% know how to swim. -30% of those surveyed were non-white and 30% were female between the ages of 25 and 50. 3 of our folks recently started jobs. For the first time ever a client's caseworker joined us. She was surprised by the lack of the drug activity other homeless service providers said existed around our program. 12 years and 1 case worker. Our program takes place 4 blocks from both St Joseph's and the LDS Temple At one point during Tai Chi there were 5 police vehicles with lights on monitoring the activity at the back entrance to the library. 3 SLC security officers watched. At the same time, at least 3 SLC security people and an additional 5 police officers were in City Hall protecting the Mayor and staff. 4 Library security staff were also on duty inside the library. Arrests 0. Individuals briefly talked to: 1 Approximate cost to the taxpayers for this approximately 1 hour period: $9,500.00 The cost of working with 25-30 homeless folks in our program for the same time period: $100.00 All this police activity took place less than 1/2 block from and in sight of, SLCPD Headquarters and the Mayor's Office. 70% of the people in our program have thought about or attempted suicide. To our knowledge, no one (0) in our program has ever committed suicide. The suicide rate for the rest of Utah has always been high nationally (top 5) and has increased by at least 10% over the past year. The average number of times people in our program have been arrested is 10. The number of times we've had to reach out to SLCPD in 12 years: 0 Numbers not only tell a story... they are the story. I wonder if a wider study will confirm what we found. Who is homeless in Salt Lake City and why are they staying homeless? Bernie

subject: FY2025-2026 Federal Funding Public Comment - Ruff Haven Crisis Sheltering
comment: Hello! My name is Lexey Payne, I am writing today to make a public comment on potential funding for Ruff Haven Crisis Sheltering for the 2025-2026 period. I have been a board member with Ruff Haven since 2021. My involvement with the board came after I was one of the clients served in Ruff Haven's first year as an organization. I am writing today to make clear the importance of Ruff Haven and the support that it offers to our community. I personally experienced a traumatic ending to an abusive relationship and ended up with nowhere to live. I found somewhere to stay temporarily while I found a new lease and got back on my feet but I was unable to take my two cats with me to stay there. My abusive ex had already left with our dog who I still have never seen again to this day, the thought of losing my cats as well was enough to tear me apart entirely. I searched for a week trying to find someone who could take care of my cats for just a little while so that I could find somewhere to live. I was completely out of luck until the last minute when I found Ruff Haven online. I sent in a request form and they took my cats into their facility the next business day. They were matched with a foster home that took extremely good care of them. I received pictures and updates regularly, and kept in touch about my ability for reunification. Knowing my cats were being taken care of as well as they would be with me brought so much peace to my worry and allowed me to focus on getting back on my feet. My cats stayed with Ruff Haven for one month until I found a new apartment. Shortly after reunification I joined the board in order to bring real life client experience to our lens. In the time since Ruff Haven assisted me I am now no longer homeless (I actually own a house now!), have finished my Bachelor's degree and begun a Master's program, become an advocate for human and animal services, and have Ruff Haven to thank for all of it. The assistance that Ruff Haven was able to offer me saved my life. I was at a critical turning point where my life could have turned into a constant road of uphill battles but instead turned into something so gratifying and beautiful. Ruff Haven doesn't just work to rehome pets to keep them off of the street, they do everything they can to assist with the core issues as to why people surrender their pets to shelters. Homelessness is one of the biggest reasons why people need Ruff Haven's services, we all know how much of an issue of homelessness we experience in Salt Lake. Ruff Haven helps people in our community to get back on their feet after something traumatic which helps to prevent people from getting trapped in the life-long cycle of homelessness that normally occurs after the first instance. I know this message is a little long so I will end with this, Ruff Haven is essential to making Salt Lake City a place where people can come together and discover the true meaning of community. I urge you to include Ruff Haven in the federal funding disbursements for this period. I don't think you will regret the good that can be done with the funding when placed in the hands of an organization that prioritizes our community so deeply. Thank you, Lexey Payne Board Member Former Client Salt Lake City Resident
